title: Session warmup, credential cache, and pullstream simplifier (cross-SDK)
author: Asha Menon
release_notes: Adds opt-in credential warmup and client-side cache for short-lived tokens; introduces a compact pullstream simplifier for cross-SDK ergonomics; bumps python/ts/go SDK versions. No breaking API changes; migration guidance provided.
description: Motivation: Production services observed several first-request spikes when a cold client performed authentication and immediately opened streaming pullstreams. This PR introduces a small, opt-in 'session warmup' surface that lets SDKs pre-warm credential caches and perform a lightweight connect handshake to reduce tail latency and first-request auth churn. Summary of changes: 1) SDK surface: add SessionWarmup API (Py/TS/Go) - opt-in, non-blocking helper that primes the credential cache and optionally establishes a minimal stream handshake; 2) Credential cache: lightweight in-memory LRU with TTL-aware entries and a single-worker refresher to avoid thundering-herd on token rotation; 3) Pullstream simplifier: a compact adapter for consumers that hides reconnect/backoff plumbing behind a single async iterator/async generator with sane defaults and explicit retry presets (short/balanced/steady); 4) Backoff presets: introduce documented backoff profiles that map to platform telemetry labels and are pluggable by advanced users; 5) Cross-SDK parity: ensure Python/TypeScript/Go have the same semantic surface for warmup and retry presets; 6) Tests & docs: unit/integration tests added; Quickstart examples and changelog entries included. Key design notes: - Warmup is non-mandatory and does not change default behavior. It is safe to call from server initialization paths. - Credential cache is intentionally tiny by default (max 8 entries) and primarily targets short-lived delegated tokens. Long-term credential storage remains out-of-band. - Pullstream simplifier is implemented as an adapter: consumers can opt-in to the simpler facade or use the full-featured streaming client. - Telemetry: warmup and cache hits/misses are instrumented with existing SDK metrics so ops can correlate warmup usage with latency improvements. Migration notes: - No required changes for existing users. - To opt in, call SessionWarmup.prime() during application startup. - For TypeScript consumers using older import paths, see the compat shim in sdk/typescript/compat/pullstream-bridge.ts Checklist: - [x] Py/TS/Go implementation and unit tests - [x] Integration test against local runtime canary - [x] Documentation and Quickstart example - [x] Telemetry events and metrics labels - [x] Version bumps (py: 2.13.0, ts: 3.7.0, go: 1.5.0) Related work: ENG-9421 (investigate cold-auth latency), ENG-10333 (streaming ergonomics epic).
